body.rationale: The IPS is still a draft, so I weigh compliance as provisional evidence and not as final. I vote for portfolios the CIO can build from: ones that pass the hard limits and rely on the covariance structure more than on fragile return forecasts, in line with the late-cycle finding in §4.3. First is resampled_efficient_frontier. It has no hard breaches. Its effective N of 13.3 is the most diffuse of the compliant return-optimised names, and the BL reviewer confirmed its numbers are internally consistent. Its weaknesses are thin drawdown headroom (-24.3% against -25%) and a muddled description of the gamma tuning. Neither is a flaw in the portfolio itself. Second is black_litterman. It has no breaches and 6.1 effective assets, and it discloses the tuning candidly. The reviewer found the mechanism claim does not follow from the specification, so it ranks below the resample. Third is pc_researcher. It has the best ex-ante Sharpe among the diversified names (0.51), a backtest Sharpe of 0.70, a drawdown of -10.9% and a low CRO risk score (0.33). It breaches volatility and tracking error, and reviewers noted the rationale was not reconciled with the solved result. That is a documentation fix, not a portfolio defect. Fourth is max_sharpe. It has no breaches, but 46% sits in us_value on one judged value-versus-growth gap, and drawdown is -24.7%. It is a useful input but should not be leaned on alone. Fifth is cvar_minimization. It has no breaches and a tail-aware objective that does not assume symmetry. Its weaknesses are fitting to a handful of crises and being tuned to the volatility floor. My first choice beats my fifth because the resample is diffuse and has no breaches and its numbers were verified, while CVaR minimisation is concentrated (effective N of 2.9) and rests on about 20 tail months. I flag hierarchical_risk_parity. It is 92% cash, breaches return, volatility and tracking error together, and its reviewers said cash as an ordinary clustering node decides the outcome. Its description of 'risk budgets' was also technically wrong. It gives the CIO little to build from. I did not flag adversarial_diversifier, since its orthogonality is valuable in an ensemble.
